Definitions

Throughout this policy, "you" and "your" refer to the Named Insured shown in the Declarations and that person's spouse if a resident of the residence premises. "Insured" means you and the following residents of your household: (a) your relatives; (b) other persons under the age of 21 who are in the care of any person named above. "Residence premises" means the dwelling, other structures, and grounds where you reside, as shown in the Declarations.

"Occurrence" means an accident, including continuous or repeated exposure to substantially the same general harmful conditions, which results, during the policy period, in bodily injury or property damage. "Bodily injury" means bodily harm, sickness, or disease, including required care, loss of services, and death that results. "Property damage" means physical injury to, or destruction of, tangible property, including loss of use of that property.

Section I – Property Coverages

Coverage A – Dwelling
We cover the dwelling on the residence premises shown in the Declarations, including structures attached to the dwelling. We also cover materials and supplies located on or next to the residence premises used to construct, alter, or repair the dwelling or other structures.

Coverage B – Other Structures
We cover other structures on the residence premises, set apart from the dwelling by clear space. This includes structures connected to the dwelling only by a fence, utility line, or similar connection. We do not cover other structures used in whole or in part for business purposes.

Coverage C – Personal Property
We cover personal property owned or used by any insured while it is anywhere in the world. At your request, we will cover personal property owned by others while the property is on the portion of the residence premises occupied exclusively by an insured. For purposes of this coverage, personal property includes, but is not limited to, furniture, clothing, appliances, electronics, and household goods. Special limits apply to certain categories of property, as shown below.

**SECTION I – CONDITIONS**

**A. Policy Period and Territory.**  
This policy applies only to losses occurring during the policy period shown on the Declarations Page and within the territory described in the policy. Any loss occurring before the effective date or after the expiration date is not covered, except as otherwise provided by law or by an endorsement attached to this policy.

**B. Your Duties After a Loss.**  
In the event of a loss to covered property, you must:

1. Give prompt notice to us or our agent.  
2. Notify the police if the loss is caused by theft or vandalism.  
3. Protect the property from further damage. If you make reasonable and necessary temporary repairs to protect the property, we will reimburse you for the cost of those repairs. You must keep a record of all expenses incurred for such repairs.  
4. Prepare an inventory of damaged personal property, showing the quantity, description, actual cash value, and amount of loss for each item. Attach all bills, receipts, and related documents to the inventory.  
5. Cooperate with us in the investigation of the claim and, when requested, provide us with all pertinent records and documents we request.  
6. Submit to examination under oath, if requested, and sign and swear to the examination.  
7. As often as we reasonably require, show us the damaged property and permit us to inspect the property and take samples of damaged property.  
8. Send us a signed, sworn proof of loss within 60 days after our request. The proof of loss shall state the time and cause of loss, the interests of all persons in the property, the actual cash value and amount of loss, any encumbrances on the property, and any other information we request.

**C. Loss Settlement.**  
Coverage for the dwelling and other structures is provided on a replacement cost basis, subject to the following conditions:

1. We will pay the cost to repair or replace the damaged property with material of like kind and quality, without deduction for depreciation, but not exceeding the limit of liability shown on the Declarations Page.  
2. We will not pay on a replacement cost basis for any loss until the damaged property is actually repaired or replaced. You may make a claim for the actual cash value of the loss at the time of loss and, if you later repair or replace the property, you may make an additional claim for the amount by which the replacement cost exceeds the actual cash value.  
3. If the damaged property is not repaired or replaced within 24 months of the date of loss, we will settle the loss on an actual cash value basis. This period may be extended by written agreement between you and us.  
4. For personal property, we will pay the actual cash value of the property at the time of loss, but not exceeding the limit of liability shown on the Declarations Page.

**D. Appraisal.**  
If you and we fail to agree on the amount of loss, either party may demand an appraisal of the loss. In this event, each party will select a competent and impartial appraiser within 20 days of the demand. The two appraisers will select an umpire. If they cannot agree upon an umpire within 15 days, either party may request that a judge of a court of record in the state where the residence premises is located select an umpire. The appraisers will separately state the actual cash value and the amount of loss to each item. If they fail to agree, they will submit their differences to the umpire. An itemized written award agreed to by any two of the three will determine the amount of loss. Each party will pay its own appraiser and bear the other expenses of the appraisal and umpire equally.

This policy applies only to losses occurring during the policy period shown on the Declarations Page and within the territory described in the policy. Any loss occurring before the effective date or after the expiration date is not covered, except as otherwise provided by law or by an endorsement attached to this policy.

**B. Your Duties After a Loss.**  
In the event of a loss to covered property, you must:

1. Give prompt notice to us or our agent.  
2. Notify the police if the loss is caused by theft or vandalism.  
3. Protect the property from further damage. If you make reasonable and necessary temporary repairs to protect the property, we will reimburse you for the cost of those repairs. You must keep a record of all expenses incurred for such repairs.  
4. Prepare an inventory of damaged personal property, showing the quantity, description, actual cash value, and amount of loss for each item. Attach all bills, receipts, and related documents to the inventory.  
5. Cooperate with us in the investigation of the claim and, when requested, provide us with all pertinent records and documents we request.  
6. Submit to examination under oath, if requested, and sign and swear to the examination.  
7. As often as we reasonably require, show us the damaged property and permit us to inspect the property and take samples of damaged property.  
8. Send us a signed, sworn proof of loss within 60 days after our request. The proof of loss shall state the time and cause of loss, the interests of all persons in the property, the actual cash value and amount of loss, any encumbrances on the property, and any other information we request.

**C. Loss Settlement.**  
Coverage for the dwelling and other structures is provided on a replacement cost basis, subject to the following conditions:

1. We will pay the cost to repair or replace the damaged property with material of like kind and quality, without deduction for depreciation, but not exceeding the limit of liability shown on the Declarations Page.  
2. We will not pay on a replacement cost basis for any loss until the damaged property is actually repaired or replaced. You may make a claim for the actual cash value of the loss at the time of loss and, if you later repair or replace the property, you may make an additional claim for the amount by which the replacement cost exceeds the actual cash value.  
3. If the damaged property is not repaired or replaced within 24 months of the date of loss, we will settle the loss on an actual cash value basis. This period may be extended by written agreement between you and us.  
4. For personal property, we will pay the actual cash value of the property at the time of loss, but not exceeding the limit of liability shown on the Declarations Page.

**D. Appraisal.**  
If you and we fail to agree on the amount of loss, either party may demand an appraisal of the loss. In this event, each party will select a competent and impartial appraiser within 20 days of the demand. The two appraisers will select an umpire. If they cannot agree upon an umpire within 15 days, either party may request that a judge of a court of record in the state where the residence premises is located select an umpire. The appraisers will separately state the actual cash value and the amount of loss to each item. If they fail to agree, they will submit their differences to the umpire. An itemized written award agreed to by any two of the three will determine the amount of loss. Each party will pay its own appraiser and bear the other expenses of the appraisal and umpire equally.

Summary of Claim

You reported water intrusion in the basement and first-floor living areas
following heavy rainfall on the night of April 17-18, 2026. Our adjuster,
Dana Reyes, inspected the property on April 20, 2026, and observed standing
water in the finished basement, water staining on the lower portions of the
drywall in the family room, and saturation of the carpet and padding. An
engineering evaluation of the property was completed on April 28, 2026, by
Midwest Structural Diagnostics. The engineering report identified the
source of the water intrusion as a failure of the sump pump discharge line
at the point where it connects to the pump unit, which allowed water to
back up into the basement during the storm event.

Coverage Determination

Based on our review of the materials in your file, including the initial
inspection report, the engineering evaluation, the sump pump receipt you
provided on May 7, 2026, and your statement of loss, we have determined
that the water damage is a covered loss under the terms of your homeowner's
policy, Policy No. HO-4482-9917.

Specifically, we have concluded that the failure of the sump pump discharge
line was a sudden and accidental discharge of water from within the
plumbing system. The policy provides coverage for direct physical loss
caused by such a discharge, subject to the terms, conditions, and
exclusions of the policy. The heavy rainfall on the night in question
contributed to the volume of water that entered the sump pit, but the
proximate cause of the damage was the failure of the discharge line, not
the rain itself. Surface water flooding remains excluded under your
policy, but that exclusion does not apply to the facts of this loss, as the
water entered the structure through the failed discharge line rather than
through the foundation or other openings.

**3. Additional Recommendations**

- **Insulation Upgrade:** The pipe that burst is located in an exterior wall with insufficient insulation. It is strongly recommended that the insulation in this wall cavity be upgraded to R-13 or higher when the drywall is replaced. This will reduce the risk of a similar freeze event in the future. This work is not included in the current estimate and would be an additional cost.
- **Pipe Insulation:** It is also recommended that foam pipe insulation be installed on the cold-water supply lines in all exterior walls. This is a low-cost preventive measure that can be completed during the repair process.
- **Drip Faucets:** During periods of extreme cold, the homeowner is advised to let the kitchen faucet drip slowly overnight. This keeps water moving through the line and reduces the chance of freezing.
- **Shut-Off Valve Location:** The homeowner was shown the location of the main water shut-off valve and the individual shut-off valve for the kitchen sink. It was recommended that the homeowner familiarize all household members with these locations in case of an emergency.

**4. Warranty Information**

All repair work performed under the original estimate (dated July 16, 2026, Job #2026-0714-01) is covered by Plumber's Choice LLC's standard one-year labor warranty. This warranty covers defects in workmanship related to the repair of the burst pipe in the kitchen exterior wall, including the replacement of the affected section of ½-inch copper supply line and the re-securing of the pipe within the wall cavity.

The warranty period begins on the date the repair work is completed and the final invoice is paid in full. The homeowner will receive a written warranty certificate upon completion of the job.

**The following items are NOT covered under the labor warranty:**

- Damage caused by freezing after the repair is complete, if the homeowner has not followed the preventive measures outlined in Section 3 of this report (insulation upgrade, pipe insulation, and drip faucet recommendations).
- Damage caused by improper use of the plumbing system, including but not limited to excessive water pressure.
- Damage caused by third-party work performed on the plumbing system after the date of our repair.
- Damage caused by normal wear and tear, corrosion, or pre-existing conditions not related to the repair.

**Manufacturer's Warranty on Parts:**

The replacement copper pipe, fittings, and solder used in this repair are covered by the manufacturer's warranty. The copper pipe carries a 50-year limited warranty against defects in material and manufacture. The brass shut-off valve installed on the kitchen sink supply line carries a 5-year manufacturer's warranty. Copies of the manufacturer warranty documents will be provided to the homeowner at the time of the final invoice.

---

**5. Maintenance Recommendations**

To ensure the long-term integrity of the repaired line and the overall plumbing system, the following maintenance schedule is recommended:

- **Annual Inspection:** Have a licensed plumber inspect the supply lines in all exterior walls before the start of the winter season (October or November). This inspection should include checking for signs of corrosion, loose fittings, and adequate insulation.
- **Water Pressure Check:** Verify that the home's water pressure regulator is functioning correctly. The recommended residential water pressure is between 40 and 60 psi. If the pressure exceeds 70 psi, it can put undue stress on pipes and fittings. The homeowner can purchase a simple pressure gauge that attaches to an outdoor spigot for this check.
- **Sump Pump Maintenance:** Although the sump pump is not related to this repair, the homeowner was reminded that the pump should be tested twice a year by pouring a bucket of water into the sump pit. The discharge line should also be checked for obstructions, especially before the spring thaw. A service record for the sump pump is maintained by the homeowner.
- **Water Heater Inspection:** The water heater, located in the basement, should be flushed annually to remove sediment buildup. This is a simple procedure that can extend the life of the unit.

---

**6. Follow-Up Recommendations**

---

**7. Summary of Diagnosis**

The cause of the water damage to the kitchen and adjacent dining room was a burst pipe in the exterior wall behind the kitchen sink. The pipe burst due to freezing, which was made more likely by the insufficient insulation in the wall cavity. The initial failure occurred during the extreme cold spell in late January 2026. The leak went undetected for a period of time, allowing water to saturate the wall and subfloor. The homeowner's sump pump and its operation were investigated and ruled out as a cause of this incident.
